@@ -919,4 +929,105 @@ mod ComposeRealSum do
   def to_cap("ref") := Ref
   def to_cap("tag") := Tag
   def to_cap(_) := Val
+
+  # ── self-CHECKING gate: numeric mix (ADR-0035, P3) ─────────────────────────────
+  # The THIRD build-loop gate (after exhaustiveness + capability) — the one that turns
+  # the self-built compiler from self-COMPILING into self-CHECKING. It reuses the
+  # equivalence-locked `Checker.num_mix` (checker.rian, locked by
+  # checker_nummix_fixpoint_test): a `d_func` whose body provably mixes int and float in
+  # a `+`/`-`/`*` is REFUSED with `{:type_error, name}` — a value never silently becomes
+  # a float. Scoped to `d_func` (the inline `def f(p T) R := body` form); separate-clause
+  # functions carry their param types in a sibling `d_sig` and are conservatively skipped
+  # (a documented tail — the gate never false-rejects them, so v1==v2 is unaffected).
+  def first_num_mix(decls Vec(Tuple)) String
+  def first_num_mix([]) := ""
+  def first_num_mix([{:d_func, _, name, params, _, _, body} | rest])
+    if func_mixes(params, body) do
+      name
+    else
+      first_num_mix(rest)
+    end
+  end
+  def first_num_mix([{:d_mod, _, inner} | rest]) := mod_mix(first_num_mix(inner), rest)
+  def first_num_mix([_ | rest]) := first_num_mix(rest)
+
+  def mod_mix(inner String, rest Vec(Tuple)) String
+    if inner == "" do
+      first_num_mix(rest)
+    else
+      inner
+    end
+  end
+
+  # lower the body to driver Core, project it onto checker.rian's Core, and ask the
+  # locked `Checker.num_mix` under the clause's typed-param env (an empty `ic`: a mix
+  # whose operand is a call to a float-returning function is the documented `ic` tail).
+  def func_mixes(params Vec(Tuple), body Tuple) Bool
+    tenv := param_tenv(params)
+    Checker.num_mix(to_chk_block(lower_body(desugar_interp(tenv, body))), tenv_dict(tenv), Prim.map_new())
+  end
+
+  def tenv_dict(Vec(Tuple)) Dict(String, String)
+  def tenv_dict([]) := Prim.map_new()
+  def tenv_dict([{n, t} | rest]) := Prim.map_put(tenv_dict(rest), n, t)
+
+  # ── driver Core → checker.rian Core projection (for `Checker.num_mix`) ──────────
+  # The driver's Core has 18 constructors and shapes (CIf over Blocks, Arm with a guard,
+  # CDot/CRemote/CStruct/CMap, …) that checker.rian's leaner Core lacks. `num_mix` only
+  # needs to (a) FIND `+`/`-`/`*` nodes and (b) infer their DIRECT operand types — so the
+  # mix-bearing nodes (CBin/CUnary, the leaves, real `__prim_*` CCalls) are preserved with
+  # checker's shape, while every structural node is collapsed to a `CCall("__x",
+  # children)` that `num_mix` still walks. The collapse uses only the driver's OWN Core
+  # constructors (whose runtime tags coincide with checker's for the preserved nodes), so
+  # the result types as `Core` AND never invents a CBin — it can therefore never cause a
+  # false rejection (v1==v2-safe). An operand that is itself an `if`/`case`/block infers
+  # `unknown` under the collapse — the gate is merely more conservative there, never wrong.
+  def to_chk(Core) Core
+  def to_chk(CNum(s)) := CNum(s)
+  def to_chk(CStr(s)) := CStr(s)
+  def to_chk(CChar(c)) := CChar(c)
+  def to_chk(CId(x)) := CId(x)
+  def to_chk(CAtom(_)) := CStr("")
+  def to_chk(CUnary(op, x)) := CUnary(op, to_chk(x))
+  def to_chk(CBin(op, l, r)) := CBin(op, to_chk(l), to_chk(r))
+  def to_chk(CCall(f, args)) := CCall(f, to_chk_all(args))
+  def to_chk(CLambda(_, body)) := CCall("__lam", [to_chk(body)])
+  def to_chk(CApply(callee, args)) := CCall("__apply", [to_chk(callee) | to_chk_all(args)])
+  def to_chk(CTuple(es)) := CCall("__tuple", to_chk_all(es))
+  def to_chk(CList(es, tail)) := CCall("__list", cat_core(to_chk_all(es), to_chk_tail(tail)))
+  def to_chk(CIf(c, t, e)) := CCall("__if", [to_chk(c), to_chk_block(t), to_chk_block(e)])
+  def to_chk(CCase(scrut, arms)) := CCall("__case", [to_chk(scrut) | to_chk_arms(arms)])
+  def to_chk(CDot(obj, _)) := to_chk(obj)
+  def to_chk(CRemote(_, _, args)) := CCall("__remote", to_chk_all(args))
+  def to_chk(CStruct(_, flds)) := CCall("__struct", to_chk_flds(flds))
+  def to_chk(CMap(flds)) := CCall("__map", to_chk_flds(flds))
+
+  def to_chk_all(Vec(Core)) Vec(Core)
+  def to_chk_all([]) := []
+  def to_chk_all([e | rest]) := [to_chk(e) | to_chk_all(rest)]
+
+  def to_chk_block(Block) Core
+  def to_chk_block(Block(stmts)) := CCall("__blk", to_chk_stmt_exprs(stmts))
+
+  def to_chk_stmt_exprs(Vec(Stmt)) Vec(Core)
+  def to_chk_stmt_exprs([]) := []
+  def to_chk_stmt_exprs([SBind(_, e) | rest]) := [to_chk(e) | to_chk_stmt_exprs(rest)]
+  def to_chk_stmt_exprs([STypedBind(_, _, e) | rest]) := [to_chk(e) | to_chk_stmt_exprs(rest)]
+  def to_chk_stmt_exprs([SExpr(e) | rest]) := [to_chk(e) | to_chk_stmt_exprs(rest)]
+
+  def to_chk_arms(Vec(Arm)) Vec(Core)
+  def to_chk_arms([]) := []
+  def to_chk_arms([Arm(_, _, blk) | rest]) := [to_chk_block(blk) | to_chk_arms(rest)]
+
+  def to_chk_tail(Tail) Vec(Core)
+  def to_chk_tail(TClose) := []
+  def to_chk_tail(TTail(e)) := [to_chk(e)]
+
+  def to_chk_flds(Vec(SFld)) Vec(Core)
+  def to_chk_flds([]) := []
+  def to_chk_flds([SFld(_, v) | rest]) := [to_chk(v) | to_chk_flds(rest)]
+
+  def cat_core(Vec(Core), Vec(Core)) Vec(Core)
+  def cat_core([], ys) := ys
+  def cat_core([x | xs], ys) := [x | cat_core(xs, ys)]
 end

+defmodule Rian.ComposeTypeGateFixpointTest do
+  # async: false — loads the verified ports + the driver into the VM.
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: false
+
+  alias Rian.Beam
+
+  # P3 — the SELF-CHECKING gate is WIRED into `build`. The composed compiler already
+  # refused non-exhaustive (`{:non_exhaustive, _}`) and BEAM-illegal (`{:not_beam_legal,
+  # _}`) programs; this adds the third gate — TYPE checking via the equivalence-locked
+  # `Checker.num_mix` (checker.rian, ADR-0035). The self-built compiler now REFUSES an
+  # int↔float program (`{:type_error, name}`) instead of silently emitting it — the step
+  # that turns the bootstrap loop from self-COMPILING into (partially) self-CHECKING.
+  #
+  # Scope (honest): the gate runs on `d_func` bodies (the inline `def f(p T) R := body`
+  # form). Separate-clause functions carry their param types in a sibling `d_sig` and are
+  # conservatively skipped — a documented tail, asserted below — so the gate never
+  # false-rejects them and the v1==v2 fixed point is unaffected.
+
+  setup_all do
+    {:ok, _} = Beam.load(File.read!("compiler/lexer_v2.rian"), :"Elixir.LexerV2")
+    {:ok, _} = Beam.load(File.read!("compiler/decl.rian"), :"Elixir.Decl")
+    {:ok, _} = Beam.load(File.read!("compiler/beam.rian"), :"Elixir.Beam")
+    {:ok, _} = Beam.load(File.read!("compiler/exhaust.rian"), :"Elixir.Exhaust")
+    {:ok, _} = Beam.load(File.read!("compiler/cap.rian"), :"Elixir.Cap")
+    {:ok, _} = Beam.load(File.read!("compiler/checker.rian"), :"Elixir.Checker")
+    {:ok, drv} = Beam.load(File.read!("compiler/compose_real_sum.rian"), :rian_type_gate)
+    {:ok, drv: drv}
+  end
+
+  defp uniq(prefix), do: :"#{prefix}_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
+
+  describe "the type gate is WIRED into build — an int↔float program is REJECTED" do
+    @mixes [
+      "def f(a Int64) Float64 := a + 1.5",
+      "def f(a Int64, b Float64) Float64 := a * b",
+      "def f(c Char) Float64 := c + 1.5",
+      "def f(x Float64) Float64 := 1 + x"
+    ]
+
+    test "compile_module and build REFUSE every numeric-mix d_func (raise {:type_error, name})",
+         %{drv: drv} do
+      for src <- @mixes do
+        assert catch_error(drv.compile_module(src, uniq(:TypeBad))) == {:type_error, "f"},
+               "the type gate did not refuse: #{inspect(src)}"
+
+        assert catch_error(drv.build(src, uniq(:TypeBad))) == {:type_error, "f"},
+               "build did not refuse: #{inspect(src)}"
+      end
+    end
+
+    test "a well-typed d_func still compiles + runs", %{drv: drv} do
+      m = drv.build("def f(a Int64) Int64 := a + 1", uniq(:TypeOk))
+      assert m.f(41) == 42
+    end
+
+    test "same-kind float arithmetic is NOT a mix — compiles", %{drv: drv} do
+      m = drv.build("def f(a Float64) Float64 := a - 1.0", uniq(:FloatOk))
+      assert m.f(3.5) == 2.5
+    end
+
+    test "untyped params infer `unknown` — conservatively NOT rejected", %{drv: drv} do
+      # `a`/`b` have no declared type, so the operands are `unknown`; the gate is
+      # conservative and never rejects on an unprovable mix.
+      m = drv.build("def f(a, b) Int64 := a + b", uniq(:Conservative))
+      assert m.f(2, 3) == 5
+    end
+
+    test "div/rem are not mix operators — an Int÷Int compiles", %{drv: drv} do
+      m = drv.build("def f(a Int64) Int64 := a div 2", uniq(:DivOk))
+      assert m.f(9) == 4
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "documented boundary — the gate is scoped to d_func" do
+    test "a SEPARATE-CLAUSE function with a mix is NOT caught (the d_sig/d_clause tail)",
+         %{drv: drv} do
+      # `def f(a Int64) Float64` (a d_sig) + `def f(a) := a + 1.5` (a d_clause) carries the
+      # same int↔float mix, but the gate only inspects inline `d_func` bodies — so this
+      # compiles today. Widening the gate to correlate a d_sig's param types with its
+      # d_clause bodies is the next increment; asserted here so the boundary is explicit.
+      m = drv.build("def f(a Int64) Float64\ndef f(a) := a + 1.5", uniq(:ClauseTail))
+      assert m.f(2) == 3.5
+    end
+  end
+end
